Level 3 · Advanced · Week 2

Objects: Blueprints and Things

A class is a blueprint; objects are the things you build from it, and each one keeps its own data.

What you will learn

  • Write a class with __init__, attributes and methods.
  • Make many objects from one class and change one without changing the others.
  • Use self correctly (and fix code that forgets it).
  • Paint turtle art with a list of objects.

The big idea

A class is a blueprint, like a cookie cutter. An object is a thing made from the blueprint, like one cookie. Every object made from the same class has the same kinds of facts, but its own values.

Anatomy of a class

Every part has a job

class Pet:                          # 1. the blueprint (capital P)
    def __init__(self, name):       # 2. setup: runs when a pet is made
        self.name = name            # 3. attributes: facts it remembers
        self.hunger = 5

    def feed(self):                 # 4. a method: an action
        self.hunger = self.hunger - 3   # MY hunger goes down

pip = Pet("Pip")                    # 5. make an object
pip.feed()                          # 6. ask it to do something
print(pip.hunger)                   #    prints 2

TipWhat is self?

self means “this object” or “my”. When you write pip.feed(), Python runs feed with self set to pip. So self.hunger is Pip’s hunger. Every method needs self as its first parameter, and every attribute is written self.something.

From dictionary to class

In Level 2 you might have written pip = {"name": "Pip", "hunger": 5}. A dictionary holds the facts. A class holds the facts and the actions, all in one place, so you can make 100 pets that all know how to feed().

Exercise2.1: Pet Class

Folder: week02/ex-pet-class. __init__ and feed are done. Finish:

  • play(): happiness +2+2 (max 10) and hunger +1+1 (max 10).

  • mood(): "hungry" if hunger ≥7\geq 7, else "happy" if happiness ≥7\geq 7, else "bored" if happiness ≤3\leq 3, else "okay".

  • describe(): returns "Pip the dragon feels okay."

Predict first: after pip.play() twice, what are Pip’s hunger and happiness? (blank to fill in)
What is Bo’s hunger? (blank to fill in)

Exercise2.2: Bubble Art

Folder: week02/ex-bubble-art. Each Bubble object remembers x, y, size and color. Finish __init__, grow, move, the big dot in draw, and make_bubbles, which returns a list of objects:

bubbles = make_bubbles(40)     # a list of 40 Bubble objects
for bubble in bubbles:
    bubble.draw(pen)           # each one draws itself

Done looks like: a black window full of bubbles, each with a white shine. Check with check_my_work.py, then commit your picture’s code in git-quest.

TipKind design

Our pets never get sick, run away or say “you forgot me!”. Good games are fun because you want to play, not because they make you feel guilty. When you design a game, ask: “Is this fair and kind to the player?”

Reflect

Pick something from a game you like. Write it as a class: its name, 3 attributes and 2 methods.

What does self mean, in your own words?

New words

class
A blueprint that says what facts and actions a kind of thing has.
object
One thing made from a class, with its own values. Also called an instance.
attribute
A fact an object remembers, like self.hunger .
method
A function that lives inside a class, like feed(self) .
__init__
The setup method (“dunder init”). It runs when a new object is made.
self
Inside a method: “the object that is running this code”, or “my”.

Homework: Objects: Blueprints and Things

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreCoin Purse (about 10 minutes)

  1. Open week02/hw-coin-purse/starter.py in Thonny. A CoinPurse object keeps a player’s coins.

  2. Finish add (ignore 0 or negative amounts), can_afford and spend (only pay if you can afford it; return True or False).

  3. Run it. The last line should be Found 7 coins! Now: 9 coins.

  4. Copy your file into Documents/git-quest and commit it with a helpful message.

Predict: purse = CoinPurse(10), then purse.spend(4), then purse.spend(7). What does the second spend return, and how many coins are left? (blank to fill in)

ChallengeDesign a class on a card

Choose a thing from a game: a spaceship, a plant, a door, a monster. Fill in its class card. Then, if you have time, write it in Python with __init__ and two methods, and make two objects.
